title: The Box Model: Foundation of Layout

scenes.say: Ever wonder why your layout breaks or elements overflow? What actually controls the size of every box on your page?

scenes.label: Box
scenes.sub: Every HTML element is a box with content, padding, border, and margin.
scenes.say: Every HTML element is a box. It has content in the middle, surrounded by padding, a border, and margin on the outside.
Let’s break it down. Content is your text or image. Padding adds space inside the border. Border wraps the padding. Margin is space outside the border.
Here’s a typical box. The total width isn’t just 200 pixels. You add padding, border, and margin.

scenes.question: How do you set a box’s total width?
scenes.right: You must account for padding, border, and margin. Or use box-sizing: border-box.
scenes.say: Interview trap: Setting width alone doesn’t control the total size. You must include padding, border, and margin—or use box-sizing border-box.
